citations.title: R.I. Gen. Laws § 44-18-7.1(g), software definitions
citations.quote: “Prewritten computer software” means “computer software,” including prewritten upgrades, that is not designed and developed by the author or other creator to the specifications of a specific purchaser.

notes: Rhode Island taxes prewritten software (delivered or vendor-hosted), not custom software or programming services, which are not among the services in § 44-18-7.3. Custom software resold to someone other than the specific purchaser becomes prewritten. Earliest date: ADV 2018-38's definition. 2026-11-02: cited page moved from http://webserver.rilegislature.gov/Statutes/TITLE44/44-18/44-18-7.1.htm to https://webserver.rilegislature.gov/Statutes/TITLE44/44-18/44-18-7.1.htm.

summary: Custom modifications to prewritten software, charged separately, are not taxable in Rhode Island.

citations.title: R.I. Gen. Laws § 44-18-7.1(g), software definitions
citations.quote: provided, however, that where there is a reasonable, separately stated charge or an invoice or other statement of the price given to the purchaser for such modification or enhancement, such modification or enhancement shall not constitute “prewritten computer software.”

notes: The code's 'charged separately' meets the statute's condition. The statute text read is current; the date is ADV 2018-38's, which quotes the same definition of prewritten software. 2026-11-02: cited page moved from http://webserver.rilegislature.gov/Statutes/TITLE44/44-18/44-18-7.1.htm to https://webserver.rilegislature.gov/Statutes/TITLE44/44-18/44-18-7.1.htm.

summary: Prewritten software is taxable in Rhode Island at 7%, on media or delivered electronically (electronic delivery since October 1, 2011).

citations.title: RI Division of Taxation ADV 2018-38 (September 4, 2018, rev. September 13, 2018)
citations.quote: Pre-written computer software delivered electronically or by “load and leave” became subject to Rhode Island sales and use tax October 1, 2011.

citations.title: R.I. Gen. Laws § 44-18-7, Sales defined
citations.quote: computer software delivered electronically or by load and leave

notes: Software on tangible media was taxable before 2011; the rule starts at the date both delivery forms were taxable. 2026-11-02: cited page moved from http://webserver.rilegislature.gov/Statutes/TITLE44/44-18/44-18-7.htm to https://webserver.rilegislature.gov/Statutes/TITLE44/44-18/44-18-7.htm.

summary: Vendor-hosted (remotely accessed) prewritten software was not taxable in Rhode Island before October 1, 2018.

citations.title: RI Division of Taxation ADV 2018-38 (September 4, 2018, rev. September 13, 2018)
citations.quote: Effective October 1, 2018, vendor-hosted prewritten computer software will become subject to Rhode Island sales and use tax

notes: Earliest date: the advisory's issue date; the advisory says the tax newly applies from 2018-10-01, so SaaS was untaxed before, but earlier text was not read.

summary: Vendor-hosted (remotely accessed) prewritten software is taxable in Rhode Island at 7% from October 1, 2018.

citations.title: RI Division of Taxation ADV 2018-38 (September 4, 2018, rev. September 13, 2018)
citations.quote: On and after that date, the sale, storage, use, or other consumption of vendor-hosted prewritten computer software, sometimes referred to as “software as a service”, or SaaS, will be subject to Rhode Island’s 7 percent sales and use tax.

citations.title: R.I. Gen. Laws § 44-18-7, Sales defined
citations.quote: The sale, storage, use, or other consumption of vendor-hosted prewritten computer software

summary: No local sales tax applies to this code in Rhode Island beyond the statewide 1% meals and beverage tax already in the RI rule.

citations.title: R.I. Gen. Laws § 44-18-18.1, Local meals and beverage tax
citations.quote: This local meals and beverage tax shall be administered and collected by the division of taxation

citations.title: R.I. Gen. Laws § 44-18-18.1, Local meals and beverage tax
citations.quote: at a rate of one percent of the gross receipts

notes: Rhode Island has no local sales tax parts in the rate data: its 1% local meals and beverage tax is statewide and collected by the Division of Taxation, and is included in the RI rule's 8%. This rule exists because the schema requires an RI:local rule beside a special-rate RI rule; no local part is ever charged. 2026-11-02: cited page moved from http://webserver.rilegislature.gov/Statutes/TITLE44/44-18/44-18-18.1.htm to https://webserver.rilegislature.gov/Statutes/TITLE44/44-18/44-18-18.1.htm.
